set.approach: Park at the large Bear Lake lot at the end of the Bear Lake road and take the trail toward Dream and Emerald lakes as far as Nymph Lake. Just past the lake, where the trail turns toward Dream Lake, the small cliff rises above the trail on the right; the flow at its far left end is this one. A short side track leads up to the base, and the gully on the left gives access to the top for a top rope.
set.descent_text: Parties walk down the ramp beside the flow, rappel from the large tree at the top, or carry on up the thin low-angle ice above to the top of the cliff.

review.notes: One route page gives the descent options and the cliff location; area page gives the trail line to the lake. No counts used.

set.approach: Park at the large Bear Lake lot at the end of the Bear Lake road and take the trail toward Dream and Emerald lakes as far as Nymph Lake. Beyond the lake, where the trail turns toward Dream Lake, the cliff rises above the trail on the right. The route is the second flow from the left end, a short distance right of the leftmost line.
set.descent_text: Parties walk down the ramp, rappel from the large tree, or continue up the low-angle thin ice to the top. Moving left to the tree near the top is also described.

review.notes: Route page for location and descent options; area page for trail.

At the far end of the lake the trail swings sharply left; leave it there and cut right a short way to the cliff. The line is the second ice flow from the right end of the cliff, just left of a small overhang and a tree.

review.notes: Approach only: route page does not say how parties get down.

At the far end of the lake the trail swings sharply left; leave it there and cut right a short way to the cliff. The route is among the lines left of Urinalysis in the middle of the cliff and is reached by angling in from the right over mixed ground.

set.approach: Park at the large Bear Lake lot at the end of the Bear Lake road and take the trail toward Dream and Emerald lakes as far as Nymph Lake. At the far end of the lake the trail swings sharply left; leave it there and cut right a short way to the cliff, where the trail meets the slightly overhanging rock. The line is the right-hand of two bolted mixed starts there.
set.descent_text: From the tree at the top of the route, walk off or rappel.

review.notes: Route page gives location and walk-off or rappel.

set.approach: Park at the large Bear Lake lot at the end of the Bear Lake road and take the trail toward Dream and Emerald lakes as far as Nymph Lake. At the far end of the lake the trail swings sharply left; leave it there and cut right a short way to the cliff. The route is on the right side of the cliff, where a broader area of ice can be linked in several ways.

review.notes: Approach only; the page names top anchor trees but not a descent.

set.approach: From the Bear Lake lot, take the Flattop Mountain trail around the lake's right side and, at the first big switchback, bear left where the Bierstadt Lake trail splits off. When the trail gains the ridge, contour right on the signed route toward Lake Helene, Fern Lake and Odessa Gorge. Standing on Lake Helene's north shore, gaze down into the gorge to spot the flows under Notchtop. Grace Falls is the wide flow in the gorge below the mountain. Avalanche terrain is possible here, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Approach from area page, matched by the route page. Route page's descent remark is too vague to use.

set.approach: From the Bear Lake lot, take the Flattop Mountain trail around the lake's right side and, at the first big switchback, bear left where the Bierstadt Lake trail splits off. When the trail gains the ridge, contour right on the signed route toward Lake Helene, Fern Lake and Odessa Gorge. Standing on Lake Helene's north shore, gaze down into the gorge to spot the flows under Notchtop. Hot Doggie hangs beneath the north face of Notchtop. A thin, steep slab pitch to a ledge is sometimes used as an approach pitch to reach the ice.
set.descent_text: Parties get off by rappelling.

review.notes: Route page: location under Notchtop's north face and a rappel descent; area page: trail line.

set.approach: From the Bear Lake lot, take the Flattop Mountain trail around the lake's right side and, at the first big switchback, bear left where the Bierstadt Lake trail splits off. When the trail gains the ridge, contour right on the signed route toward Lake Helene, Fern Lake and Odessa Gorge. Standing on Lake Helene's north shore, gaze down into the gorge to spot the flows under Notchtop. The route is down and to the right of the Guide's Wall, at the first main ice curtain, and starts up a slight ramp to reach it.
set.descent_text: Descend by V-thread, or walk off.

review.notes: Route page gives V-thread or walk-off and the start position; walk-off option not tried by the author.

set.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge parking area, using snowshoes or skis as needed, and follow the summer trail line to the Shortcut without taking it. Turn right (west) up an unnamed drainage until it is easy to bear south back onto the main trail close to where the Loch Vale trail branches off, then head west keeping to the left branches to the log bridge over Glacier Creek. Stay right along the creek to Mills Lake, cross the lake southward and continue across Jewell Lake, then follow the valley bottom toward Black Lake. A large boulder stands on the left of the trail a little past Jewell Lake; from there go straight west over and around windfall and across Glacier Creek. The ice is plainly visible on the slope above the creek. This is avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast. Cave is the shorter left side of the crag, beside the ice cave.
set.descent_text: Rappel from either of two trees with rings, one just above the ice cave and one on the left side of the flow, or scramble off to the left.

review.notes: Area page for the approach; route page for crag layout and descent options.

set.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge parking area, using snowshoes or skis as needed, and follow the summer trail line to the Shortcut without taking it. Turn right (west) up an unnamed drainage until it is easy to bear south back onto the main trail close to where the Loch Vale trail branches off, then head west keeping to the left branches to the log bridge over Glacier Creek. Stay right along the creek to Mills Lake, cross the lake southward and continue across Jewell Lake, then follow the valley bottom toward Black Lake. A large boulder stands on the left of the trail a little past Jewell Lake; from there go straight west over and around windfall and across Glacier Creek. The ice is plainly visible on the slope above the creek. This is avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast. Center is the broader right side of the crag.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the tree with rings on the left side of the flow, or walk off to the right.

review.notes: Area page for the approach; route page for crag layout and descent options.

set.descent_text: The climb ends in easy scrambling terrain up a short gully. From the top of that gully, the descent couloir heading north toward Sky Pond is easy to spot, and it drops to the lake.

review.notes: Route page: top-out and north couloir descent to Sky Pond (stated in both description and location). Approach not written: page gives the face, not a walk-in.

set.approach: Park in one of the turnouts above Glen Cove on the Pikes Peak toll road, near the closed dirt road that carries the trail. The trail follows the ridge south and descends into the Oil Creek drainage, a fork of French Creek, and finishes at the tunnel. The climb is on the north-facing wall beside the tunnel mouth, reached by walking the trail from the road. It has a near-vertical left-hand flow and a lower-angle ramp on the right, and both lead to an upper shelf of ice.

review.notes: Area and route pages agree on the road-side parking and trail. Route page shows WI2+ while the stored grade is WI3-4; same single route in the area. No descent stated.

set.approach: Use the signed winter parking area on the Ophir road, across from the town maintenance garage, and take the track at its east end downhill to the creek and a bridge. Cross the bridge, leave the track, and work south-southeast up the creek's east bank to the falls in a small amphitheater. The walk is short; snowshoes help once snow piles up.
set.descent_text: Tie off to trees above the ice and rappel, or walk around the canyon on the left.

review.notes: Single route page for approach and descent; area page for the Ophir road.

set.approach: From the CO 145 turnoff, follow the Ophir road to the pullout near the yellow 10 mph sign. Take the summer trail up the boulderfield into Cracked Canyon and follow it to the top of the canyon, where the main flow hangs. The canyon floor is loose, so move carefully, and if you cannot see the upper ice from the road the route is probably not in.

review.notes: Approach only; route page gives the parking and the trail up the canyon; no descent stated.

set.approach: From Breckenridge, take Spruce Creek Road to the Mohawk Lakes trailhead, parking as high as the road allows, then follow the trail past the abandoned mining works to Lower and Upper Mohawk Lakes. The route is the pair of couloirs on the right side of the north face; it is easiest to pass the lakes on their south ends to avoid marsh on the north. The meadow ends at the foot of the face, and the final climb to its base is a long, steady uphill.
set.descent_text: Descend as for the peak itself, by the east ridge. Cornices overhang the west ridge above the route.

review.notes: Both pages from one site; route page states the east ridge descent; area page the trail. No numbers used.

set.approach: From the Blue Lakes trailhead (the 850 Road west of CO 9 near Breckenridge, to the parking area below the dam), a walking trail leads directly to the ice crag on the slope below Quandary's southwest face. Bourbon Beaver is the largest flow on the crag; from the grassy flats below, walk up the low-angle ice to the base of the lowest step.
set.descent_text: Walk off to the right down talus and scree.

review.notes: Route page: base and walk-off; area page: trail from trailhead.

set.approach: From the Blue Lakes trailhead (the 850 Road west of CO 9 near Breckenridge, to the parking area below the dam), a walking trail leads directly to the ice crag on the slope below Quandary's southwest face. Trucksicle is at the left end of the crag and is the steepest sizeable ice as you approach; from the grassy flats, walk up the talus slope to the left to reach it.

review.notes: Approach only; route page does not give a clear descent.

set.approach: Drive County Road 850 to the upper Blue Lake dam and park. The climb sits right over the lower Blue Lake, below a big mine building, and an old mule trail climbs through the scree to its base. Please keep clear of the cabin and road beside the lake. This slope is avalanche prone, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route or downclimb.

review.notes: Route page for location and descent; area page for access.

set.approach: Drive County Road 850 to the upper Blue Lake dam and park. Cross the stream and traverse the scree and talus slope on the south side of the valley to the base, keeping clear of the cabin and road at the lower lake. A mine shaft sits at the base of the right-hand start and can be hidden by drifted snow. The area is avalanche prone, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Scramble off to the west, or rappel the route.

review.notes: Route page for approach details and descent; area page for access.

set.approach: Drive County Road 850 to the upper Blue Lake dam and park. The route is directly above the lower Blue Lake, beside some old mine buildings on the cliffs, and the walk in is short when the road is open. The area is avalanche prone, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Walk off the top of the second pitch back down to the first pitch belay, then rappel to the base.

review.notes: Route page for approach and descent; area page for access.

set.approach: Drive County Road 850 to the upper Blue Lake dam and park. Cross the stream and traverse the scree and talus to the base; the route shares its start with North Star. Keep clear of the cabin and road beside the lower lake. A mine shaft sits at the base of North Star's right-hand variation and may be hidden by snow. The area is avalanche prone, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: From the upper pitches you can walk off west down scree and talus. Otherwise rappel from the fixed anchor near the top of the fifth pitch to the ledge anchor, then straight down to the bolted anchor of a summer sport route, which reaches the ground.

review.notes: Route page for shared start and descent; area page for access.

set.approach: The route starts in Wheeler Basin. A good way in is from the Monarch Lake trailhead up the Arapaho Pass trail to the basin. From there follow the line of least resistance up the long couloir that ends at a notch on the ridge; the couloir is easy to pick out from Caribou Pass in spring. Check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: The couloir can be downclimbed. The alternative is to carry gear over the notch and descend the Navajo snowfield on the far side, which is a long way round.

review.notes: Single route page for start, notch end, and both descent options. Page is in Alpine Rock tree and describes a WI3 step in a chimney consistent with AI3-4.

set.approach: From Governor Basin the walk in is brief but over loose scree. The route climbs the highest point of the pinnacled ridge between Mendota Peak to the south and Mount Emma to the north, and it starts by climbing the gully toward an east-facing offwidth crack.
set.descent_text: Rappel the summit block, then make a second rappel from a narrow alcove on the east side where the pinnacle meets the ridge, landing at the foot of the snow gully.

review.notes: Route page for descent and line; area page for the Governor Basin approach.

set.approach: From Ridgway take CO 62 west, turn left on the Dallas Creek road, and follow it south to the Blue Lakes trailhead. Follow the Blue Lakes trail through a big clearing and into the band of trees under the east face of the peak informally called S4, then leave the trail and climb southwest toward the face. The ice is in a shaded corner, facing right, beside a deeply recessed couloir to its left; steepening snow leads to its base. This is avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: V-thread where the ice ends, or climb a little higher and rappel from bushes or small trees.

review.notes: One route page for approach and descent; no counts used.

set.approach: From Ridgway take CO 62 west, turn left on the Dallas Creek road, and follow it south to the Blue Lakes trailhead. Follow the Blue Lakes trail to the meadow beyond the stream crossing, from where the ice shows in a cleft high on the northeast face of S4. Leave the trail and go straight up the avalanche track to a knoll, then up the wide apron to a hidden gully on the right and through it to the base of the ice. Avalanche and rockfall hazard are both serious here, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route on double-rope V-threads or fixed gear. A further rappel can spare some steep snow downclimbing. Alternatively, if the snow is good, climb on to the summit of S4, descend its easy south gully and hike east down the basin to the Blue Lakes trail.

review.notes: One route page for approach and descent; rappel counts left out.

set.approach: From Ridgway take CO 62 west, turn left on the West Dallas Creek road and follow it through the ranch land to Box Factory Park. From the gate at the northwest end of the meadow, hike the Dallas Creek trail, then leave it for an old road along an irrigation canal and keep to old road cuts, staying north and west of the creek and aiming for the north cirque of S9. In the meadow below the cirque, look up and left for the ice on the lower northeast face, then use an old road that runs beneath the face and kick up steep snow to the ice. Expect rockfall from the face above the belay.

review.notes: Approach only; page does not describe how parties get down.

set.approach: From Ridgway take CO 62 west, turn south on CR 7 and drive to the East Dallas trailhead. Hike south, bearing left almost at once onto the Dallas Trail, and later take a sharp right to stay on it. Watch ahead for a prominent band of cliffs holding the climb, then leave the trail and bushwhack up the drainage to the slot where Wilson Creek leaves Blaine Basin.
set.descent_text: Once the creek flattens, you can head east and hike down the Blaine Basin trail. To return to the foot of the slot, go north-northwest to a steep gully with an anchor in place and rappel through the trees.

review.notes: One route page; numbers omitted.

set.approach: From Ridgway, drive CR 5 past Miller Mesa to the Wilson Creek trailhead, then walk east along the same road a short way to the second drainage crossing, the creek that comes off Corbett's north face and meets Coal Creek below the road. Follow the drainage up by the easiest line to the ice at the foot of the north face. The slope above is avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Belay from trees at the top and walk off to either side.

review.notes: Route page for approach and walk-off.
